title: AMOS: Active Mining with Observable Steps for Agenda-Driven Review Knowledge Discovery

problem.claim: Review-based decisions are agenda-relative because different agendas define different evidence, thresholds, and rules.

gap.claim: Existing methods do not execute agenda-specific decision logic or ground verdicts in cited reviews, while end-to-end LLM prompting risks hallucinations.

contributions.claim: The paper formulates Agenda-Driven Review Knowledge Discovery (ARKD).

AMOS is a two-phase framework in which ASC compiles natural-language agendas into deterministic Agenda Specs and TEKOA uses prioritized retrieval, LLM verification, and Bayesian-calibrated early stopping.
AMOS produces auditable verdict traces for agenda-driven review analysis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On ARKD-Bench built from Yelp data, AMOS skips 26% of reviews.
AMOS improves Macro-F1 by up to 47% over the strongest LLM baseline.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online reviews support consumer decisions, but decision criteria vary by agenda.
Existing approaches lack agenda-specific logic and cited-review grounding, and end-to-end prompting can hallucinate.
The paper formulates ARKD and introduces AMOS with deterministic agenda compilation and cost-aware verification.
On a Yelp-derived benchmark, AMOS skips reviews, improves Macro-F1, and provides auditable traces.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates broad lightweight retrieval from focused costly verification.

interpretation.claim: Staged processing can allocate expensive reasoning to prioritized candidates instead of applying it uniformly.

application.claim: Agenda-driven review systems may benefit from retrieval-first pipelines with explicit verification stages.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this allocation strategy generalizes beyond the reported setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark size, agenda distribution, or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not provide details needed to independently verify the reported results.
